title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
statement: Given the level-order array of a Binary Search Tree and an integer k (1-indexed), return the kth smallest value in the tree.
hints: Inorder traversal of any BST visits nodes in ascending sorted order.
Collect non-null values via inorder DFS or filter & sort.
Return the element at index k - 1.

solutions.title: Inorder Array Collection
Early-Stopping Inorder DFS

editorial.approach: An in-order traversal (Left, Root, Right) of a Binary Search Tree visits values in strictly non-decreasing sorted order. Perform an iterative in-order traversal using an explicit stack: traverse as far left as possible, then pop the node, decrement k, and if k == 0, return that node's value. Otherwise advance to its right child.
editorial.why_optimal: Stops early as soon as the kth element is reached, running in O(H + k) time instead of visiting all N nodes, using O(H) stack space.
editorial.pitfalls: Collecting all elements into an array before indexing, which wastes O(N) memory and forces traversing the entire tree even when k = 1.
